concept.body: Interior-region cheat sheet: ALTERNATE interior angles (opposite sides of the transversal) are EQUAL; CO-INTERIOR / same-side interior angles are SUPPLEMENTARY (sum 180°). Opposite side → equal; same side → add to 180. Check the side first.

explanationVariants: Alternate interior angles (opposite sides) are equal, so 80° pairs with 80°.
Opposite sides of the transversal between the parallels means equal: 80°.

widget.prompt: Across two parallel lines, the ALTERNATE INTERIOR partner of an 80° angle measures how many degrees?

commonErrors.feedback: 100° = 180 − 80 is the SAME-side (co-interior) partner. ALTERNATE (opposite-side) interior angles are EQUAL: 80°.
10° = 90 − 80 is a complement, not a transversal pair. Alternate interior angles are equal: 80°.

steps.body: One transversal cutting two **parallel** lines makes eight angles — but only two distinct sizes. Every angle is either the base size a or its supplement 180 − a. The named pairs just tell you WHICH: **corresponding** and **alternate** angles are EQUAL; **same-side (co-interior)** angles are SUPPLEMENTARY.

widget.prompt: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. Sort each angle pair by its relationship.

items.label: corresponding angles
items.feedback: Corresponding angles sit in the SAME position at each crossing — always equal across parallels.

items.label: alternate interior angles
items.feedback: Alternate interior angles are on opposite sides of the transversal, between the lines — equal across parallels.

items.label: co-interior (same-side interior) angles
items.feedback: Same-side interior angles together span a straight-line configuration — they SUM to 180°.

items.label: alternate exterior angles
items.feedback: Alternate exterior angles mirror the alternate interior ones on the outside — also equal.

widget.missFeedback: Alternate and corresponding pairs are EQUAL; same-side (co-interior) pairs are SUPPLEMENTARY.
widget.successFeedback: Equal for corresponding/alternate; supplementary for same-side.

explanationVariants: Corresponding angles across parallel lines are equal, so the partner of 70° is 70°.
Same position at each crossing = corresponding = equal measure: 70°.

widget.prompt: A transversal crosses two parallel lines; one angle is 70°. Its CORRESPONDING angle measures how many degrees?

commonErrors.feedback: 110° = 180 − 70 is the SUPPLEMENT — that's a same-side or linear-pair relationship. Corresponding angles are EQUAL: 70°.
20° = 90 − 70 is a complement, not a transversal relationship. Corresponding angles are equal: 70°.

steps.body: The interior region — between the two lines — holds the pairs students mix up most. **Alternate interior** (opposite sides of the transversal) are EQUAL; **co-interior / same-side interior** (same side) are SUPPLEMENTARY. Opposite sides ⇒ equal; same side ⇒ sum to 180°. That one distinction settles most problems.

widget.prompt: Across two parallel lines, an angle of 55° has an ALTERNATE INTERIOR partner. What does the partner measure, in degrees?

commonErrors.feedback: 125° = 180 − 55 is the CO-INTERIOR (same-side) partner. ALTERNATE interior angles are on opposite sides — EQUAL: 55°.
35° = 90 − 55 is a complement, not an angle-pair rule. Alternate interior angles are equal: 55°.

explanationVariants: Same side of the transversal, between the lines — they add to a straight angle, 180°.

widget.prompt: Across the same parallels, the CO-INTERIOR (same-side interior) partner of a 55° angle measures how many degrees?

commonErrors.feedback: 55° would make them EQUAL — that's the ALTERNATE interior relationship. Same-side interior angles are SUPPLEMENTARY: 180 − 55 = 125°.
305° = 360 − 55 uses a full turn. Co-interior angles fill a straight angle: 180 − 55 = 125°.

steps.body: One transversal fact anchors the rest: **corresponding angles are equal** (the Corresponding Angles Postulate for parallel lines). From it, alternate and co-interior relationships all FOLLOW by pairing with vertical angles and linear pairs — which is exactly what the next lesson proves.

widget.prompt: You KNOW corresponding angles are equal. Which additional fact lets you conclude alternate interior angles are equal too?

options.label: a corresponding angle and an alternate interior angle are vertical angles
options.feedback: The alternate interior angle is the VERTICAL angle of a corresponding one — and vertical angles are equal, so the chain closes.

options.label: alternate interior angles are given equal in the problem
options.feedback: You're trying to PROVE they're equal, so you can't assume it. The link is through vertical angles.

options.label: all eight angles are equal
options.feedback: Only HALF the angles share each size — the others are supplements. Alternate interior equality comes via one vertical-angle step, not all-equal.

options.label: the transversal is perpendicular
options.feedback: A perpendicular transversal makes every angle 90° — a special case. The general link is vertical angles.

hints: The given angle is 112°. Which listed angle is its EQUAL, and which is its SUPPLEMENT?
Corresponding and alternate angles equal 112°; same-side and linear-pair angles equal 68°.
Find the angle that must be 68° — the co-interior partner.
explanationVariants: 112° repeats at every corresponding and alternate position; its supplement 68° appears at every same-side and linear-pair position. The co-interior partner is 180 − 112 = 68°.
Only two sizes exist: 112° (corresponding/alternate) and 68° (its supplement). The same-side interior angle is the 68° one.

widget.prompt: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. One interior angle is 112°. What is its CO-INTERIOR (same-side interior) partner, in degrees?

commonErrors.feedback: 112° is the ALTERNATE interior partner (opposite side, equal). The SAME-side partner is supplementary: 180 − 112 = 68°.
248° = 360 − 112 uses a full turn. Co-interior angles fill a straight angle: 180 − 112 = 68°.

takeaways: A transversal on parallels makes just two angle sizes: a and 180 − a.
Corresponding and alternate pairs are EQUAL; same-side (co-interior) pairs are SUPPLEMENTARY.
Corresponding-angles is the anchor; the rest follow via vertical angles and linear pairs.
steps.teaser: Next: prove the alternate interior angles theorem — corresponding angles plus one vertical-angle step.
